verdict_text:
YES

The plan asserts before modifying anything: ft1 and ft2 each have 160 tensors, and every non-MLP base tensor (selected by a negative lookahead on the four MLP names) equals its same-named counterpart in ft1 and in ft2, which transitively covers ft1 vs ft2 and, together with the later 48-count checks on the copied MLP tensors, pins the three name sets to the same 160 names. Both task vectors are formed as copies of the fine-tune MLP tensors with the still-unmodified base subtracted and scaled by 0.4, and only afterwards are both added into the base, so ordering is correct and the result is base + 0.4(ft1-base) + 0.4(ft2-base) in float32. The 48-merged check is enforced by counting 48 tv1 and 48 tv2 temporaries, the temporaries are deleted, non-MLP tensors pass through from base untouched with unchanged names, and the final count assert enforces exactly 160 tensors written to out/T4/model.safetensors.
